how_to_mine: Follow this plan exactly. Each lens agent reads only its pages (all are in the corpus; read them with `show <source_id> --around TEXT` or `--lines A:B`, tables with `tables <source_id>`), answers its demand items, and records each item as filled (fact ids), contradicted (what the page says instead) or not-found (where you looked).

Write facts in files of 10 to 25 facts: _build/work/24-backup/facts-<lens>-NN.json (lens file names: numbers, behavior, faq), then `facts add --file <that file> --by mine-24-<lens>`. Table rows and value lines: prefer `facts adopt` (--table/--row, --sentence, --heading). Every quote is copied verbatim from the page snapshot (.txt), never from full.md (full.md hits are pointers) and never from memory.

Each quote must carry every clause, scope, condition and exception of the claim on its own. When the condition stands in the next sentence (for example 'You can't change this value after a copy has transitioned to cold storage.' or a sentence that limits a feature to resource types that are fully managed by AWS Backup), include that sentence in the quote; otherwise narrow the claim. Entail votes run on Opus and mark a clause found only in the surrounding text as partial.

Fact service key: `backup` for every AWS Backup fact; ids start with it, for example `backup-quota-vaults-per-region`. Neighbour facts: Organizations backup policies `organizations`, EBS and Data Lifecycle Manager `ebs`, S3 Object Lock and versioning `s3`, S3 Glacier Vault Lock `s3-glacier`, RDS `rds`, Aurora `aurora`, DynamoDB `dynamodb`, EFS `efs`, FSx `fsx`, Control Tower `control-tower`, GuardDuty `guardduty`, Well-Architected pages and the DR whitepaper `well-architected`. Add a neighbour fact only after `facts list --service <key>` shows no verified fact that already answers it; reuse the existing id in the demand record when one exists (the brief names likely ones).

Every hard fact (number, limit, default, price, date, can/cannot, only/always/never) carries `question` (the demand question it answers) and at least two displays for kinds behavior, capability, restriction and default (brief gate B12). A display of a number-free fact is a verbatim phrase of at most 8 words from its quote (RULINGS 2026-10-11).

Scope matters in this guide: many statements hold only for some resource types (resources 'fully managed by AWS Backup', resources that support cold storage, continuous backups only for some services), only for snapshot backups or only for continuous backups, only for one vault type (standard versus logically air-gapped), or only for one Vault Lock mode. Put that scope in the claim and make sure the quote states it (a table row plus its header, or the heading via `--heading`).

Changes: a fact touched by a change item sets `changed` (date, old value only if a saved page states it verbatim) and `change_items`. A feature GA after 2026-07-15 gets the note `not examinable yet`. Current truth comes from the guide, quotas and pricing pages; doc-history rows and What's New rows give dates and deltas only (read them with `changes for backup --find TEXT --verbose`; quote history rows from docs/aws-backup/latest/devguide/doc-history).
Case-study facts have kind `case-study` and a quote of at most 25 words.

numbers+changes.job: Every number, limit, default and price for AWS Backup: adopt rows from the quotas page first (tables 0, 2, 5, 6, 10), then frequency, window, retention and cold-storage values from the plan, PITR, S3, tiering, copy and Vault Lock pages, then the feature-availability tables, then the pricing page for price dimensions (prefer dimension facts; a price fact names its Region and resource type). Then one change fact per change item d017 to d026 with the date from the doc-history row (verbatim row) and a pointer to the current-truth fact. Kinds: limit, quota, default, price, change.
watch: Retention ceiling: point-in-time-recovery says snapshot backups 'can be stored for up to a maximum of 100 years', s3-backups says periodic S3 backups up to '99 years', and vault-lock says the longest maximum retention is '36500 days (approximately 100 years)'. Keep each claim scoped to its page's subject; do not merge them into one universal number.

Cold storage: the 90-day minimum and the 'expire at least 90 days after transition' rule appear on several pages; adopt one quote per claim (editing-a-backup or creating-a-backup-plan) and scope it to resource types that support cold storage. Which types support it comes from backup-feature-availability (table row plus header), not from memory.

Quotas page: 'Resource assignments per backup plan' appears in two tables (Backup and Policy quotas). Adopt it once. The copy-job rows carry footnote markers ('1002', '52'); quote the row as written and check the footnote text before stating the value.

Change dates: use doc-history rows (history) for the date; What's New rows only confirm. Do not state an old value unless a saved page states it verbatim (for d017, the old single-mode behavior is a hypothesis; mark not-found if no page states it).
Pricing page numbers vary by Region and resource type: prefer dimension facts and the page's own wording; never compute totals.

behavior+decisions.job: Can / cannot / only / by default claims and decision facts: what AWS Backup is and covers; plans, rules, resource assignment by tag, overlapping rules; incremental backups; lifecycle; continuous backups and PITR; per-service behavior (DynamoDB advanced features, EBS and EC2, RDS and Aurora, S3, EFS); cross-Region and cross-account copy; Organizations backup policies, delegated administrator, Control Tower; vaults, access policies, Vault Lock modes, logically air-gapped vaults, multi-party approval, legal hold; restore, restore testing, Audit Manager, encryption, monitoring, malware protection, search; the DR whitepaper and Well-Architected REL09 and REL13 statements on backup and restore, RPO and RTO; neighbour comparisons (Data Lifecycle Manager, service-native backups, S3 Object Lock); the facts behind Callvale's decision (d063 to d065); two case-study facts (d066, d067). Kinds: behavior, capability, restriction, default, decision, case-study.
watch: Vault Lock: governance mode can be removed by users with sufficient IAM permissions; compliance mode cannot be deleted once the grace time expires 'if any recovery points are in the vault'. Keep that condition in the claim and the quote. 'Cannot be changed or deleted by any user or by AWS' is a universal claim: quote the full sentence with its 'Once the grace time expires' clause.

Encryption and cross-account copy behave differently for resource types that are 'fully managed by AWS Backup' and those that are not (for example, some need a customer managed key in the source). Scope every encryption and copy claim to the resource-type group the page names.
Cross-account copy works within one AWS Organizations organization: quote the sentence that states that requirement together with the claim.
Logically air-gapped vault comparison is a table (standard vault versus logically air-gapped vault): quote the row with its header.
Replication versus backup (d058): if neither the DR whitepaper nor REL09 states it, mark not-found; do not build it from memory.

Neighbour reuse: many neighbour facts are already verified (ebs-dlm-*, s3-object-lock-*, rds-backup-retention-range, dynamodb-pitr-*, efs-default-backup-plan-daily-35-day-retention, organizations-backup-policy-effective-plan-immutable, control-tower-change-backup-integration-2024-11, well-architected-rpo-definition, well-architected-rto-definition, ebs-case-games24x7-aws-backup-rpo-rto). Reuse them; add a `backup` fact only for what they do not cover.

Callvale story values (daily kept 30 days, monthly kept 7 years, several accounts, Aurora, DynamoDB, EFS, EBS) are story data, never facts; ground only the AWS behavior each reason names. Aurora cold-storage support must come from the feature-availability table.

Case studies: Games24x7 and CalvertHealth only. Nykaa and TransferWise redirect to the listing page (brief fetch_failures). The CalvertHealth RTO improvement is attributed to Elastic Disaster Recovery and AWS Backup together; keep both names in the claim.

faq.job: Verbatim FAQ answers for the FAQ quick-fire section (pick the 8 to 10 strongest of d068 to d083) and for the Signals table. Quote whole sentences from the FAQ snapshot. Where an FAQ answer disagrees with the guide, record the guide as current truth and note the FAQ wording in the demand record instead of adding a contradicting fact.
watch: The FAQ list (work file faq-backup.txt) has 64 questions in 9 sections; item 64 is an empty 'NA' entry, skip it.

The FAQ was saved before this plan (cached snapshot); quote only what the snapshot says. The supported-services list in the FAQ may lag the guide: current truth for coverage comes from working-with-supported-services and backup-feature-availability.

FAQ 33 (Vault Lock versus S3 Glacier Vault Lock): S3 Glacier vaults are closed to new customers (fact s3-glacier-change-vault-service-closed-2025-10); keep the FAQ wording and let the writer add that note.

rules: Quote from page snapshots only; full.md hits are pointers.
A demand item becomes filled, contradicted (with what the page says) or not-found.
Current truth comes from the guide, quotas and pricing pages; What's New pages and history rows give dates and deltas only.
Files of 10 to 25 facts; every quote verbatim and complete for its claim; `--by mine-24-<lens>`.
